campaign_id: qwen35-4b-w4a16 d1: the W4A16 determinism pad at depth 3 (2026-09-09)
question: The determinism pad pads decode row counts to fixed tiers, removing the row-count dependence that was believed to flip near-tie tokens at high concurrency. It was measured on the 9B as costing throughput with no identity gain, but never on the 4B, where the pad is active at depth-3 c64 (256 decode rows) and inert at MTP0 c64 (64 rows, below the 128-row threshold).
prediction_on_record: Committed before this arm ran, in 2026-09-09-qwen35-4b-speculation-two-populations.json: 'An intervention aimed at tie-breaking can at best address the smaller part' - because only about a tenth of depth-3 c64 events are amplified intrinsic ties and 63% belong to a speculation-specific population. The expectation was therefore a small reduction at most.

arms.candidate: d1, VLLM_XPU_W4A16_DETERMINISM_PAD=1 and _PAD_HIGH=1, verified in the container environment because the engine's automatic knob check does not cover the pad
arms.otherwise_identical: one B70, TP1, depth 3, draft INT4 head, FULL_DECODE_ONLY capture 1-64, max_num_seqs 64, max_num_batched_tokens 512, 2026-08-25 suite, 20 passes per rung

identity.significance: On the oracle-free measure at c64 the two arms give about 99 and 96 minority samples of 1344, a difference of 3 against a standard deviation of roughly 14. A null.

throughput.note: The pad is inert at c32, where depth-3 decode is 128 rows and sits at the threshold, and costs 11.7% at c64 where it is 256 rows. That matches the 9B lane's -13% measurement.

sites.statement: The pad does not change which sites fire or how often. All 18 of the control's c64 sites appear in the pad arm, which adds three low-rate ones, and the per-site counts track closely: cache-c056 @50 19 against 19, cache-c048 @89 17 against 19, capacity-c062 @54 18 against 16, cache-c000 @39 16 against 18. Total events 170 against 171.
sites.why_this_is_the_strongest_part: A rate null can hide two offsetting changes. An unchanged site set with unchanged per-site counts cannot: the pad is not acting on this phenomenon at all.

finding: The determinism pad costs 11.7% of throughput at depth-3 c64 and buys nothing. Identity is unchanged on both the oracle-based and the oracle-free measure, and the fragile sites are the same sites at the same rates. Keep it off, which is what the lane already does.
why_it_fails: The pad removes row-count dependence, which is the right instrument for tie-breaking perturbed by batch shape. The two-populations result says that is at most a tenth of what happens at depth-3 c64; the majority is a speculation-specific population that the pad has no mechanism to touch. And the tie-flip half is not obviously row-count driven either - the same sites survive a reboot, two days, both compilation modes and now the pad, while flipping direction when the arithmetic itself changes under TP2.
confirms: The 9B lane's earlier reading, recorded as '-13% at c64 depth 3, no identity gain', on a second model with 20 passes per rung and an oracle-free measure.
